significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: the “Mechanism-Universality Score = fraction of the concept's variance that is cross-model reproducible” would distinguish mechanisms from shortcuts and predict OOD retention, stitching transfer, and causal relevance across scientific models. This establishes both a phenomenon—shared-subspace membership covaries with generalization—and a proposed mechanistic interpretation—dataset-independent mechanisms preferentially occupy shared representations; it would constrain whether cross-model convergence, studied more generally in Huh et al.’s 2024 Platonic Representation Hypothesis and related representation-alignment work, can serve as evidence of scientific validity rather than mere common encoding. The negative branch is also informative because failure despite independently trained models would rule out representational agreement as a general validator and show that shared artifacts or inductive biases cannot be distinguished from mechanisms this way; true and false therefore denote clear states, although “genuine mechanism” requires an external operational definition. Topic substitution lowers the assessment materially: the broad topic alone would merit only the median, while the specific score-to-OOD predictive law and its cross-domain mechanism-versus-confound consequence support the higher score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “Mechanism-Universality Score,” offered as an “annotation-free audit” and predictor of OOD generalization; its predictive use is ex ante when it is used to screen a recovered concept before trusting that concept or deploying it under distribution shift, rather than merely explaining an observed failure afterward. Unlike a model-specific direction, the claimed relationship survives recalibration: after aligning and re-extracting representations in another model, the hypothesis predicts that higher shared-subspace variance will correspond to greater OOD survival, transfer, and causal relevance. The asserted scope covers independently trained protein, molecular, and materials models with different architectures and data, giving interpretability researchers and model auditors a reusable gating metric, though the conclusion does not itself provide a validated deployment rule for scientists outside AI and shared training artifacts could limit transfer. Under the topic-substitution check, merely asking whether models represent established scientific mechanisms would not supply this score or lead-time-bearing audit handle, so the reach comes from the claim-specific cross-model predictor rather than from the scientific domain’s importance.
